LESSON: CLOTHING CONSTRUCTION PROCESSES ● MANAGEMENT OF FULLNESS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: HOME SCIENCE
Strand: Clothing and Textiles
Topic 3.5: Clothing Construction Processes ● Management of fullness
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 22

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Clothing Construction Processes ● Management of fullness, part of Clothing and Textiles in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 HOME SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: How does the type of fabric influence the management of fullness in clothing construction? 2. How is control of fullness managed in clothing construction?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify types of management of fullness used in clothing construction,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Clothing Construction Processes ● Management of fullness in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. make samples of management of fullness used in clothing construction,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Clothing Construction Processes ● Management of fullness in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. examine qualities of different methods of managing fullness in clothing construction,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Clothing Construction Processes ● Management of fullness in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. construct a simple garment using methods of managing fullness,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Clothing Construction Processes ● Management of fullness in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. embrace the use of management of fullness in clothing construction.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Clothing Construction Processes ● Management of fullness in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. embrace the use of management of fullness in clothing construction.

F. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. brainstorm on the meaning of management of fullness and write notes. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication to share their views,

2. search for information from print media, electronic devices and discuss with peers on the types of management of fullness and present in class (such as pleats, gathers, darts, elastic, easing). Learners with manipulation difficulties could be provided with adapted digital resources with appropriate accessibility features. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. brainstorm on the meaning of management of fullness and write notes. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication to share their views,
2. search for information from print media, electronic devices and discuss with peers on the types of management of fullness and present in class (such as pleats, gathers, darts, elastic, easing). Learners with manipulation difficulties could be provided with adapted digital resources with appropriate accessibility features. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Clothing Construction Processes ● Management of fullness together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: When the learner clearly describes the procedure followed when working the stitches and giving focused

feedback.

● Learning to learn: When the learner prioritizes tasks well by having a learning plan during the working of management of

fullness processes.

Values:
● Unity: Learners appreciate efforts of others when working the stitches and during peer assessment.

● Respect: Learners understand and appreciate views from others during peer assessment of the samples of management of

fullness made.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Socio-economic and environmental issues: Learners tactfully manage wastes accrued from the fabrics and threads during

stitching.

● Safety: Learners practise safety measures in the Home science workshop during stitching.

● Road Safety: Learners design and construct PPEs to enhance safety for road users.
